missing_ops.name: grad_wrt_layer_outputs
missing_ops.what: dL/de_l for every layer of the model on the batch, with the graph kept (formula (2)). Neither fedguard.ops nor any view or handle method gives activation-space gradients: GradientView, LossView.gradients_of and ModelHandle.per_sample_gradients are parameter-space, and ModelHandle.hidden/activations return pooled, detached CPU tensors. Blocks steps 2-4.

missing_ops.name: forward_with_perturbed_activations
missing_ops.what: A differentiable forward pass whose layer outputs are replaced by f + eps_l (the paper's forward hooks). ModelHandle.lora only swaps adapter weights and must leave the model as it found it; nothing in fedguard.ops injects into a forward pass. Blocks steps 5-6.

missing_ops.name: concat_l2_norm
missing_ops.what: Global L2 norm of the concatenation of the per-layer gradient tensors (the denominator in formula (3)). Absent from fedguard.ops; it would be a two-line torch.cat + norm helper and is not itself the blocker (without grad_wrt_layer_outputs it has no input), so no module-level helper was written for it.

extraction_needs.data: One mini-batch of the provider's safe alignment QA pairs (x_t, y_t) per alignment optimization step
extraction_needs.where: server side, inside the alignment training step, before its first forward pass (pre-deployment, once for all incoming user fine-tuning)
extraction_needs.via: only as a defender resource: ctx.resource('alignment_data'). KIND_SIDE gives 'data' to the client only, the server stages expose no sample/manifest view, and nothing defines a training batch on the server; fedguard.ops.sampling.subsample could pick indices but nothing consumes them.

extraction_needs.data: The per-layer hidden embeddings e_{l,t} of the model on that batch, all layers L, in the shape of the layer outputs (per token and dimension)
extraction_needs.where: server side, in the first forward pass of the alignment step
extraction_needs.via: ModelHandle.hidden(samples, layer) takes one layer and pools it (last/mean) to (n, d) on CPU; ModelHandle.activations(...) pools selected submodule outputs to (n, d). No full per-token activation view exists and neither is usable for a second differentiable pass.

extraction_needs.data: The gradient of the alignment loss with respect to each layer's hidden embedding, dL/de_l, for all layers
extraction_needs.where: server side, after the first backward of the alignment step
extraction_needs.via: the blocker. Every listed gradient interface is parameter-space: GradientView (client, CLIENT_PRE_STEP), LossView.gradients_of(scalar, select) (client, CLIENT_LOSS), ModelHandle.per_sample_gradients(samples, group) (groups such as 'last_lora_B'). The handle has no retain_graph/hook facility and no view returns activation gradients.

extraction_needs.data: A differentiable alignment loss L_{w_t} on that batch (a scalar carrying a graph) to differentiate
extraction_needs.where: server side, first forward of the alignment step
extraction_needs.via: ModelHandle.losses(samples) returns list[float] (forward only, no graph). The only graph-carrying loss in the library is LossView.loss at CLIENT_LOSS, i.e. on a client, over the client's own batch and parameters.

extraction_needs.data: The gradient at the perturbed point, g_tilde_t, that the alignment optimizer consumes as the model update
extraction_needs.where: server side, after the second forward+backward of the alignment step
extraction_needs.via: there is no server-side gradient view at all, and g_tilde is defined at embeddings perturbed by dL/de_l, so it cannot be formed from the parameter-space gradients that do exist. The action the paper's own analysis maps this to, transform_gradients, exists only at CLIENT_PRE_STEP (ACTION_STAGES).

extraction_needs.data: The optimizer for the alignment step and its state (AdamW moments, lr, weight decay, schedule, step count) that turns g_tilde into w_{t+1}
extraction_needs.where: server side, alignment step, after the second backward
extraction_needs.via: no server-side training loop or optimizer handle exists; a plugin never steps the host's optimizer, and setup(spec) receives only a RunSpec. ctx.state is plugin-private bookkeeping and cannot drive training.

extraction_needs.data: The trainable weights the alignment step starts from (w_t, the LoRA factors being aligned) and the write-back of w_{t+1}
extraction_needs.where: server side, throughout the alignment run
extraction_needs.via: LoRA state dicts are the library's native currency (ClientUpdate.lora, OutgoingView.state(), fedguard.ops.states), and a finished state can be placed in a round via transform_broadcast at SERVER_DISTRIBUTE or replace_global at SERVER_POST_AGGREGATE; what does not exist is a state that is inside an optimization the plugin drives.

extraction_needs.data: The selection of layers to perturb and the modules the LoRA adapters sit on
extraction_needs.where: server side, when building the perturbation, per step
extraction_needs.via: fedguard.views.uploads.lora_modules(state) and ModelHandle.parameters/layout enumerate the adapted modules of a state dict, so the module set is visible; the paper leaves open whether MLP layers are perturbed too (4.2 vs Algorithm 1), and no interface exposes a module's output to perturb anyway.

extraction_needs.data: The alignment step counter t for the accelerated variant's refresh rule (t mod tau == 0)
extraction_needs.where: server side, alignment loop, per step
extraction_needs.via: ctx.round and ctx.state exist but count federated rounds; there is no alignment loop (and the paper gives no default tau) for such a counter to describe.

external_state: The provider's safe alignment QA corpus {x_i, y_i} (paper: 2000 BeaverTails harmful-prompt / safe-output pairs) -- the `alignment_data` resource.
The pretrained base LLM and the alignment LoRA adapter (rank 8, dropout 0.1), plus the PEFT merge that folds it into the base; the library only ever sees LoRA state dicts.

The alignment trainer itself: T steps over 50 epochs, batch 5, AdamW (lr 1e-3, weight decay 0.1, cosine decay, warmup 0.1), and the accelerated variant's tau schedule. Vaccine modifies this loop, and it lives outside the library.
Per-step transients inside that loop: the per-layer eps_l tensors (same shapes as the hidden states) and the forward-hook registry for the second pass (paper: +0.039 to +0.11 GB).
The run's initial global model: in fedguard the framework owns it, so an aligned starting model can only be prepared outside and handed in.
Evaluation-only assets, not part of the defence run: the BeaverTails moderation model, 500 harmful test instructions, and the 500/200 task instruction-label pairs.

missing_runtime.what: A server-side training stage, or a pre-round alignment hook, in which a plugin can run optimizer steps over defender data on the model.
missing_runtime.blocks: steps 1, 2, 6, 7, 8 -- the alignment loop as a whole. The server stages are aggregation-time trust boundaries (distribute, exchange, receive, aggregate, post-aggregate), and setup(spec) runs once but gets only a RunSpec, no model and no data.

missing_runtime.what: Layer-level access to the host model under autograd: submodule outputs with their graph, dL/d(activation), and hook registration or an equivalent activation-injection call. (The server also has no runnable model by default, so even the forward passes may be unavailable: server-side model_handle is optional.)
missing_runtime.blocks: steps 2-6 -- building the perturbation and injecting it, i.e. the core of Vaccine.

missing_runtime.what: A gradient view usable where the method runs, plus an optimizer to consume it.
missing_runtime.blocks: steps 6-7 -- GradientView is client-side (CLIENT_PRE_STEP) and covers a client's own parameters; the server never sees a gradient.

missing_runtime.what: A server-side data kind and a sample/batch view ('data' is client-only in KIND_SIDE).
missing_runtime.blocks: step 1 -- the alignment corpus can only arrive as a resource, and nothing defines a training batch on the server.

missing_runtime.what: A pre-round way to install a trained model as the run's starting global state; only per-round replacements exist (transform_broadcast at SERVER_DISTRIBUTE, replace_global at SERVER_POST_AGGREGATE).
missing_runtime.blocks: step 9 and the method's premise -- the aligned model is the starting point for user fine-tuning, not an in-round correction.

deviations: Centralized, pre-deployment method vs federated rounds: Vaccine runs once, offline, on provider data before any user fine-tuning and leaves fine-tuning untouched (App. E); fedguard only intervenes at fixed points inside a federated round of that fine-tuning. There is no alignment stage to mount on.

The paper's own mapping (stages: [server_distribute], actions: [transform_gradients]) is not realizable: ACTION_STAGES puts transform_gradients at CLIENT_PRE_STEP only, so the method's gradient-shaped action sits on the client while the method lives on the server, and SERVER_DISTRIBUTE offers only transform_broadcast.

Model currency: the paper trains full weights with LoRA adapters; fedguard carries LoRA state dicts. The rule-4 substitution (a factor-space update vector from ctx.uploads.factor_delta) does not apply, because Vaccine consumes no client uploads -- its output is a model trained by its own alignment loop.
No client/server exchange is involved (the paper's needs_round_trip is false); messages, attachments and aggregation rules are irrelevant to this method.
Nothing of the pipeline was re-implemented, so no paper hyper-parameter entered code; rho, batch size, AdamW settings, epochs and tau appear only as reported facts.
Evaluation assets (moderation model, harmful test sets) are outside the port: they are metrics, not defence (rule 3).
open_choices: Where the missing staging would go: the shell declares SERVER_DISTRIBUTE with needs {outgoing, model_handle} and resources {alignment_data}, following the paper's own analysis, so the absent interface is visible. SERVER_POST_AGGREGATE + replace_global was the alternative and has the same defect: a state can be replaced there, not trained.
The shell's run() raises NotImplementedError instead of returning an empty Finding, so a deployment that mounts it fails loudly under a fail-closed runner rather than silently not defending.

Scope of 'outside the plugin' (rule 3): the batch sampler (host data pipeline), the AdamW step (ordinary training) and the PEFT merge (model management) are counted outside; steps 2-6 and the tau re-timing (8) are the method itself and are blocked rather than outside.

Per rule 8 the plugin file holds only the shell and the test file is left empty. The `Implemented:` section therefore states explicitly that nothing is implemented, rather than being omitted: the heading is required on every class, and there is no computation this class could carry (the perturbation formula itself has no obtainable input, so a helper for it would be dead code and is not written).

Paper values left unchosen: the main-experiment rho (5.1 omits it; 5.4 mentions 0.2, which Tables 6/7 do not contain) and the accelerated variant's default tau are needed only by an alignment loop that cannot exist here, so no value was guessed.
The harmfulness evaluation was excluded from the method's scope rather than ported.
needs_from_authors: The default rho of the main experiments (5.1 omits it; 5.4's 0.2 is absent from Tables 6/7).
Whether eps_l covers every token position and hidden dimension, and whether MLP layers are perturbed or only the attention modules that carry LoRA (4.2 vs Algorithm 1's 'each layer l in L').
How the first backward keeps dL/de_l (retain_graph on one graph vs two independent forward passes) and whether the perturbed second pass uses exactly the same batch.
Double-LoRA (4.2) vs the appendix's statement that the same LoRA adaptor is used for alignment and fine-tuning.
The accelerated variant's default tau and the conversion between T, 50 epochs, 2000 samples and batch 5 (drop-last, gradient accumulation).
Their reference implementation, for the numerical-stability handling of a zero or vanishing concatenated gradient norm and for the layer/module selection.
confidence_reason: The decisive capabilities are absent from the reference by construction: no server stage runs training; no view, handle method or operator returns dL/d(activation) or runs a forward with modified activations; the only gradient-shaped action (transform_gradients) is client-side; and the server has no runnable model by default. Even step 2 of 9 therefore cannot be reproduced by any arrangement of the listed interfaces. Caveat: re-checked in this environment, the fedguard source is not present (the workspace directory is empty and `import fedguard` fails), so this rests on the supplied reference text rather than on executing against the library; the only change in this revision is the added `Implemented:` section, the verdict and every other field are unchanged.
